title: Heavy rain before autumn sampling lowered English river invertebrate scores below upstream storm overflows in 2008-2024 but not above downstream ones; wetter half-years gave no overflow penalty
abstract: Question: does wet weather lower river invertebrate quality (WHPT ASPT) more below storm overflows in England? Data: 194,066 Environment Agency kick samples (1990-2025, 23,304 sites), 15,273 overflow outlet points from EDM returns 2021-2025, OS Open Rivers, Met Office district rain and E-OBS daily rain. Method: we routed sites and outlets on the river network; outlets 0-5 km upstream are the exposure and outlets 0-5 km downstream are a placebo. Models compare each site with itself and remove regional year effects. Results: (1) Pre-planned test: a wetter six-month period did not lower ASPT more below overflows; upstream and downstream terms were both slightly positive (autumn +0.016 and +0.012 per log spill hours per log rain ratio; difference +0.004, 95% CI -0.004 to +0.012), mainly before 2008. (2) With the 28-day heavy-rain exposure of sci:da41f917, the pooled 1991-2024 autumn term did not replicate (+0.0005, SE 0.0009), was positive in 1991-2007 and negative in 2008-2024 (-0.0038, SE 0.0012). In 2008-2024 the term came from upstream outlets (-0.0053, SE 0.0022, per heavy-rain day per doubling of outlets) and not downstream ones (-0.0002, SE 0.0018). It held with 10 km routing, spill hours, other fixed effects, both sub-periods and 6 of 7 regions; rain after the sample and rain 1-2 months earlier gave no upstream term. Size: about -0.06 ASPT for 6 upstream outlets and 4 heavy-rain days, 0.2 of the within-site SD. Spring was null. (3) Repeating sci:c1ad1c2a independently: reported annual spill hours (2021-2025) gave no within-site decrease, between-site ASPT was lower by 0.052 per log upstream hour against 0.012 downstream, and exposed sites did not fall behind after 2018. Limitations: associations only; outlet map from 2021-2025 applied to earlier years; the heavy-rain split was planned after the related publications and the upstream-minus-downstream contrast alone includes zero; family-level index; England only.
